result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days, defaulting to 30. The full test suite passes (`mvn -q -o test`, exit 0). I didn't add a test for the register-then-renegotiate case (45 days, then 14).

- **`model/Supplier.java`**: added a `paymentTermsDays` component. The old 5-argument constructor still works and sets the standard 30 days, so existing callers compile unchanged.
- **`schema.sql`**: new `supplier.payment_terms_days` column, `NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, checked to be 0 or more.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the payment terms, so they can be set at registration and changed later.
  - `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read and return them.

Other queries that build a `Supplier` through the 5-argument constructor still show 30 days regardless of the stored value. These include the supplier performance and spending reports and the per-product supplier lookups. I left them alone because you only asked for the supplier listings and the single-supplier lookup.
